newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends steady as higher crude supports.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends steady as higher crude supports.

text.p: NWE naphtha ended the day steady to a tad lower on Tuesday, after a rollercoaster of a day as IPE crude futures shot higher in late trade after a lacklustre start.
Naphtha swaps for April were assessed at $207.50/$208.50 a tonne, having dipped to $206/$207 in earlier trade.
A cargo was heard offered out of the U.K. at $201 cif NWE.
"The seller was looking for $202 at the beginning of the day," said one player. "I think they were set to sell it at $200 when crude futures turned round. They're looking for $201 now."
Another player with 35,000 tonnes of material in Antwerp looked set to put it into storage. "They'll probably hold onto it for May," said one trader.
Another player was heard bidding for pipeline spec material at $202 cif NWE. Traders said one player had put in offers at $205 and then $204.
Some Russian fob barrels were also heard offered at quotes low.
A number of market participants were reported to be examining the possibility of working the arbitrage door to the East following price jumps there over the past two days.
"There's plenty of material around but it's not in the Mediterranean, which is where material going East usually comes from," said one trader.
Traders said that cargoes would have to measure up to around 70-80,000 tonnes to work.
NWE end-users were reported to be looking to other materials such as LPG. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
